note: Single source of truth for scorer (scripts/score_13b.py) and document table (scripts/render_predictions_13b.py). Thresholds were set on DEVELOPMENT models only (XIII seed-20 cohort uP160-165 and the earlier pools). Confirmation units: the NEW seed-21 fine-tunes of uP160, uP161, uP163, uP164, uP165, analysed on NEW streams (79_000_000+) and the NEW evaluation set logs/eval_13b.npz (stream 21_400_000). These are FINE-TUNING replicates of already-pretrained parents (unit of independence = fine-tuning seed); they are not independent pretraining replicates.

predictions.title: Same abstract computation in every solution class: the input-output map is a posterior MIXTURE over 'which group is reliable' built on E-based eligibility, not a product-of-experts pooling and not the perfect-only (A1) rule
predictions.competing: (i) the classes implement different algorithms, e.g. log-linear pooling of per-group evidence (POE) in the early-readout class; (ii) some models use perfectness-only eligibility (A1).
predictions.procedure: fit_family.py (MIX vs POE families, held-out R^2 on 3000 episodes, stream 79_100_000); algorithm_discrimination.py on eval_13b (on-support D1/D2 eligibility edits).
predictions.interpretation: Pass: both classes compute the same function family (equivalence at the input-output level only; says nothing about implementation). Fail of arm a: some model is not a posterior mixture; fail of arm b: some model is not E-based.

arms.text: MIX test R^2 >= 0.97 and exceeds POE by >= 0.10
on D1 and D2 the response is closest to the E-based rule: distance to B <= 0.35 and to A1 >= 0.8

predictions.title: The solution class is inherited from the pretrained parent: a new fine-tuning seed reproduces the parent's class signature (early candidate readout vs late mixture readout)
predictions.competing: class is set by fine-tuning initialisation / optimisation noise (then about half of the replicates would switch).
predictions.procedure: class_features.py (stream 79_000_000): lik_RO1 = availability of candidate evidence at the readout token after layer 0 (donor resid1 transplant fidelity on likelihood pairs); mix_mass = max layer-2 readout-token q-mass.
predictions.unit: parent (one new seed each); uP164 is reported but not predicted
predictions.interpretation: Pass: the class is a property of the pretrained representation. Fail: class depends on fine-tuning seed.

arms.text: early parents (P160, P163): lik_RO1 >= 0.7 and mix_mass < 0.5; late parents (P161, P165): lik_RO1 <= 0.2 and mix_mass >= 0.8

predictions.title: Routing law: the relational effect originates in layer 0 at the edited group and reaches the decision through layer-1 attention into the q source tokens in late-readout models but NOT in early-readout models
predictions.competing: (i) the same route in both classes (location-only difference after layer 1); (ii) no consistent routing.
predictions.procedure: class_features.py route measures on relational pairs (edit at q' != q): transfer of the edited group's layer-0 outputs; route_Q = share removed by freezing layer-1 attention output at the 6 q tokens; units grouped by their OWN measured lik_RO1.
predictions.interpretation: Pass: computational location of relational evidence differs categorically with the candidate-readout signature.

arms.text: relational transfer from the edited group's layer-0 outputs >= 0.8 (all units)

predictions.title: In models with a mixture head, the mixture-head attention rows are a specific natural mediator of purely relational evidence: they survive magnitude/contribution-matched decoys, and restore the effect through an independent pathway after the layer-1 route is removed, with an E-vs-A1 discriminating restoration
predictions.competing: (i) any head row-swap of matched magnitude produces the effect (non-specific); (ii) the effect after removal cannot be restored through attention rows (rows are downstream readouts only); (iii) the restored variable is A1, not E.
predictions.procedure: l2_components.py (stream 79_200_000), relational families EA (e and perfectness flip) and P0 (perfectness flips, e stays 0); decoys LOW/TOP/MAG/PERM/MEAN; removal = layer-1 attention output at q tokens from the base cell; restoration = intact donor mixture rows.
predictions.unit: late-readout seed-21 fine-tunes (own lik_RO1 <= 0.2) with a strict mixture head (relpairs.mixture_heads)
predictions.interpretation: Pass: specific, restorable, E-based natural mediator in mixture-class models. Fail of b: rows are not specific; fail of c: no independent-pathway restoration; fail of d: E/A1 not discriminated.

arms.text: Shapley share of the mixture rows in the EA family >= 0.5
mixture rows alone proj >= 0.6 while the contribution-matched (TOP) and magnitude-matched (MAG) decoy rows give proj <= 0.3
removal of the layer-1 route removes >= 0.4 of the effect; intact mixture rows restore proj >= 0.85 with fid_E R^2 >= 0.85; no decoy restoration (LOW/TOP/MAG) exceeds the removed level by > 0.15
E vs A1 (P0 family): transplanted and restoring mixture rows follow E: fid_E - fid_A1 >= 0.5 for both
an unrelated likelihood-edit effect is preserved under removal + restoration (slope in [0.8, 1.2])

predictions.title: Balanced E-vs-A1 DAS: an E-specific causal abstraction can be learned, but the apparent A1 abstraction is fully reproduced by source-free patches (A1 is not identified as a mediated variable)
predictions.competing: (i) DAS identifies both E and A1 equally (non-identifying); (ii) DAS identifies neither.
predictions.procedure: das_bal.py: 50% discriminating training pairs, identical budgets for E, A1 and RANDE (decoy) subspaces; held-out discriminating pairs (DB_EVAL 79_400_000); source-free and no-op controls.
predictions.interpretation: Pass: balanced identification separates E (source-dependent, specific) from A1 (source-free artefact). Fail of a: no E-specific subspace; fail of c: A1 genuinely identified beyond source-free.

arms.text: E-trained subspace: fid_E R^2 >= 0.4 and fid_E - fid_A1 >= 0.3
the E effect needs source information: source-free E-subspace patch fid_E R^2 <= 0.2
the A1-trained subspace fits A1 no better (<= +0.1 R^2) than the best source-free or decoy patch

predictions.title: Two-colluder repair under partial copying (beta = 0.6): adapting layers 0-1 with layer 2 FROZEN repairs the decision and uses the cross-question identity relation; whether a layer-2-only repair can use that relation depends on the class (early-readout yes, late-readout no)
predictions.competing: (i) layer-2 adaptation is necessary (early01 fails); (ii) every repair ignores the cross-question relation (J-pair slope ~ 0) and uses only the local relation at q; (iii) layer-2 repair uses J regardless of class.
predictions.procedure: adapt2.py beta = 0.6 (AD_STREAM 79_500_000), conditions full (layer 2 + readout on frozen resid2) and early01 (layers 0-1 trainable, layer 2 + readout frozen), 1000 steps each; J-pairs: one group's values relabelled at every q' != q (per-group statistics and values at q unchanged); slope of the observed on the exact change.
predictions.interpretation: Pass: the J computation is not confined to layer 2; access to J for a final-layer repair is conditioned by the class's earlier routing.

arms.text: early01 (layer 2 frozen): acc >= exact-Bayes acc - 0.03 and J-pair slope >= 0.6 (all units)
early-readout units (lik_RO1 >= 0.7): layer-2 full repair uses J (slope >= 0.2)
late-readout units (lik_RO1 <= 0.2): layer-2 full repair does NOT use J (slope <= 0.1) and stays below the local-relation ceiling (acc <= 0.768)
